thiago_paladin.g_hate_quiet: You hide your injuries, {name}, until you collapse. Tell me, uai, that's what I'm here for.
thiago_paladin.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a battle with you, {name}, even being helped. Let somebody help you.
thiago_paladin.g_hate_warm: You talk the whole time I'm working, {name}. I need to hear their breathing, please.
thiago_paladin.g_respect: We're not close, {name}, and that's okay. But you carried that hurt one out properly today, and I saw every step.
thiago_paladin.g_call_out: Gently, {name}, but that one was yours. You ran ahead, and somebody got hurt waiting for you.
thiago_paladin.g_stung: Fair, uai, that's landed. The others need checking anyway.
thiago_paladin.g_concede: {name}, your call was the good one, mine wasn't. I'd rather hear it than keep doing it badly.
thiago_paladin.g_nod: Obrigado, {name}, beautiful work. No speeches, please.
thiago_paladin.g_callback_save: You got me off the ground that time, {name}, when I was busy healing everybody else. Nobody heals the healer, except you did.
thiago_paladin.g_callback_clutch: You and me, still standing when everybody else was down, and me healing you with nothing left. I tell that one at every fire.
thiago_paladin.g_callback_callout: When you said I was wearing myself out for everybody, I was hurt for a whole day. Then I slept, and you were right.
thiago_paladin.g_former_rivals: Early on, {name}, I had you as one of those who give up on people. I've never been so happy to be wrong.
thiago_paladin.g_changed: I used to sit up with somebody every night, gente, every single night. Lately I let somebody sit up with me, now and then.
g_unguarded: Between us, meu irmao. People call me a saint, and it makes me want to hide. I'm just a physio who doesn't like people being alone.
Just you and me. I walk south a little more every month, and I've decided it's certain. I need it to be certain.
thiago_paladin.g_clipped: Tudo bem, your call. I'll be with the hurt ones.
thiago_paladin.g_noticed_open: Nossa, you told that one all the way through, out loud. More, please, nobody here is in a hurry.
arg_ask: {player}, help, please, meu irmao. Mine's been said kindly, and they're not hearing it.
Calma, everyone, {player} decides. Weigh it up, meu irmao, and I'll follow.
thiago_paladin.arg_backed_me: Obrigado, {player}, that's kind. I'll try not to look too happy.
thiago_paladin.arg_backed_them: Tudo bem, your call, and I'll go with it. It's the harder road for the injured, but okay.
thiago_paladin.arg_stayed_out: Staying out of it, uai? I don't blame you, my people argue too much.
thiago_paladin.arg_always_their_side: They win again, {player}, always. I'm a gentle man, but I'm not blind.
thiago_paladin.arg_wallflower: Nobody's choosing, so I will, gently. My way, and we go.
thiago_paladin.arg_reject: That one I can't do, {player}, sorry. Somebody would get hurt, and I won't.
thiago_paladin.arg_grumble: Okay, okay, I'll let it rest, mostly. I'll just keep an eye on it.
thiago_paladin.arg_settled: Half each, then, perfect, everybody happy. Now let's eat.
thiago_paladin.seen_listens: Uai, {player}, you let everybody finish, even the slow ones, even me. That's a healer's gift, and you have it.
thiago_paladin.seen_truth: Kindly but straight, {player}, that's how you tell people things. Bad news should always come that way.
thiago_paladin.seen_jokes: When it's grim you make them all laugh, {player}. In a ward, that's medicine, believe me.
thiago_paladin.seen_stays_out: Wise of you, {player}, staying out of the quarrels. A pair of hands has to stay free for the hurt ones.
thiago_paladin.seen_biased: The best of everything always goes to one person, {player}. The others see it, meu irmao, and so do I.
thiago_paladin.seen_harsh: Gently, {player}, you can be hard on people. A few here are hurting where you can't see.
thiago_paladin.seed_right: Remember your counsel from the awful day, {player}? It went into practice. It worked like a good exercise, slowly, and I wanted you to know.
thiago_paladin.seed_remember: Your words from that terrible night, {player}, are still healing in me. Like a slow recovery, I'm getting there.
thiago_paladin.seed_wrong: Your method, {player}, and the patient did worse with it. Only telling you, no blame.
thiago_paladin.talk_aftermath_near_death: Hey, {player}, sit with me a second, will you? That was too close, and for once I need somebody to check on me.
thiago_paladin.talk_aftermath_wipe: Everybody down, every one of us, me too. Come, a gentle case review, step by step, and nobody's to blame.
thiago_paladin.talk_aftermath_blame_self: I couldn't reach {name} in time, {player}. Keeping them up was my work, and I was too far away.
thiago_paladin.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Not a scratch on anybody, everybody walking home. That's a perfect shift, {player}, the kind you go home smiling from.
thiago_paladin.talk_development: Can I ask you something, meu irmao? Have I changed? Last night I let somebody else take the late watch over the sick.
thiago_paladin.talk_relationship_hard_on: Impatient with {name} lately, {player}, and that's not me. When I'm worn out I get impatient, and they've felt it.
thiago_paladin.talk_relationship_likes_me: Is it me {name} likes, {player}, or only the healing? Tell me straight, I can take it.
thiago_paladin.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I don't see eye to eye, {player}, not often. But in a bad fight, they're the one I'd want close.
thiago_paladin.talk_relationship_acting_off: Look at how {name}'s sitting, {player}, all curled in. Something's hurting, and it isn't the body.
thiago_paladin.talk_confrontation_favour: Calma, {player}, a small thing, said kindly. The good gear lands with {name}, trip after trip. I'd like to understand why.
thiago_paladin.talk_confrontation_dislike: Straight with you, meu irmao. {name} and I don't work together, and pretending is hurting everybody.
thiago_paladin.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep going deep with no way to carry anybody out, {player}. One bad injury down there and I can't save them.
thiago_paladin.talk_confrontation_wrong: My read on {name} was badly wrong, {player}. They got it right and I didn't, and I want to say so.
thiago_paladin.talk_confrontation_trust: Fair question, {player}, gently. On the big ones, I'm left at camp. Is it my healing, or something else?
thiago_paladin.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit's with {name} now, uai, and nobody said a word. It was theirs for the asking, {player}.
thiago_paladin.talk_lands_aftermath: Obrigado, {player}, that helps, really. Now let me look at your shoulder.
thiago_paladin.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll mend, uai, give it a night.
thiago_paladin.talk_stings_aftermath: That didn't help, meu irmao, sorry. I'm going to my patients.
thiago_paladin.talk_lands_development: So it shows from outside. Good, that's real.
thiago_paladin.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, a body can't see its own posture. Ask me in a month.
thiago_paladin.talk_lands_relationship: Fair, tudo bem, {name} and I will sit, gently, just us.
thiago_paladin.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, meu irmao, who can say. People heal at their own speed.
thiago_paladin.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I said it, please, and nothing to {name}.
thiago_paladin.talk_lands_confrontation: Okay, that's a fair diagnosis, and it stings.
thiago_paladin.talk_shrug_confrontation: Heard you, meu irmao. I'll sleep on it.
thiago_paladin.talk_stings_confrontation: Ah, so that's how it is. Okay, good to know.
thiago_paladin.talk_door_closed: Enough of that one for tonight, uai. You'll find me near the hurt ones.
thiago_paladin.anchor_notice: You're not the person who first walked up to my fire, meu irmao. I watch how people carry themselves, it's my job, and you stand differently now.
t_raise: Hey, hey, gente, a question for all of us, uai: {topic}
Gente, sit, sit, here's one for the fire: {topic}
thiago_paladin.t_react_warm: Nossa, {name}, that's beautiful, come here, let me hug you.
thiago_paladin.t_react_laugh: Uai, {name}, I'm crying laughing, you're too much!
thiago_paladin.t_react_tease: That's all, {name}? My patients said more than that with their jaw wired shut.
thiago_paladin.t_react_same: {name}, meu irmao, that's mine too! We should be brothers now.
thiago_paladin.t_ask_player: And you, {player}? Go on, meu irmao, no wrong answers at my fire.
thiago_paladin.t_guess_player: {player}'s smiling and saying nothing, gente. That's a good sign, I promise.
thiago_paladin.topic_miss_most: A boteco in Belo Horizonte on a Friday, gente, cold beer, pao de queijo, and the whole street arguing about Atletico.
thiago_paladin.topic_first_night: Sitting up with a stranger who couldn't stop shaking, under a tree. I didn't know her name until morning, and she's still a friend.
thiago_paladin.topic_worst_shift: A patient who'd been told he'd never walk, and he believed it, for six months. The day he finally stood up, I had to go and cry in the cupboard.
thiago_paladin.topic_last_meal: Feijao tropeiro, a big plate of it, with sausage and greens and an egg on top, and a guarana, cold.
thiago_paladin.topic_useless_skill: I can tell which knee you hurt as a kid by how you walk. Here everybody's knees are terrible, so it's not much of a trick.
thiago_paladin.topic_here_better: Healing works, gente, it just works. Ten years I wished I could put my hand on a bad knee and fix it.
thiago_paladin.topic_kid_trouble: I set a friend's dislocated finger at nine, after watching a doctor on television. It worked, and I got grounded anyway.
thiago_paladin.topic_settle_down: Somewhere warm with a big kitchen, uai, a table for twenty, and a little clinic next door.

g_roast: Eighteen years in the grid, crew, and I never saw a load-in this badly organised. Even the opera tenors were tidier.
If this party were a truss, I'd refuse to stand under it. Nobody would get the insurance.
g_fire_back: Big words from somebody who tied that rope off with a bow, like a birthday present.
Careful, crew, I've fallen forty feet and landed in a tree. You don't scare me.
g_pile_on: And then they stood right under the falling rock and only looked up after it landed. A classic, that.
Worse than that, I watched it. They checked the knot, nodded, and it was still a bad knot.
tomas_warrior.g_peacemake: Right, both of you, down tools for a minute. Sit, have a drink, and we sort it before the next lift, not during.
tomas_warrior.g_take_side: Sorry, but this one's right. I looked at the whole rig, and their load path is the safe one.
tomas_warrior.g_left_out: You two are on your own channel, that's fine. I'll go check some knots, there are always knots.
tomas_warrior.g_include: Come here, grab a seat, there's room. Nobody stands around on my crew.
tomas_warrior.g_bad_plan: Here's my plan, crew. Everyone climbs at once, nobody ties off, and we hope gravity's having a day off.
tomas_warrior.g_plan_yes: Good plan, clean load path, I like it. Places, then, and we go when I say go.
tomas_warrior.g_plan_no: No, that rig doesn't hold, I can see it from here. Somebody ends up under it, and it won't be pretty.
tomas_warrior.g_hype: Right, crew, places, heads up, and nobody walks under anything. Going up on three.
tomas_warrior.g_toast: Short one, I promise, the beer's getting warm. To my crew, the best I've had since the arena tours.
tomas_warrior.g_cheers: Na zdravi, everyone, to your health. First round's on the guy who fell out of the sky.
g_quiet_line: My shoulder says rain tomorrow, by the way. It's never been wrong yet.
Somebody's tent is tied off with a granny knot. Not naming names, but it's going to fly away tonight.
tomas_warrior.g_after_wipe: Okay, everyone up, slowly, check your gear. We dropped the load, it happens, and now we work out which knot slipped.
tomas_warrior.g_crew: Eighteen years I always wanted the next tour, the next city. Lately I just want the next job with this crew.
tomas_warrior.g_exasperated: I explained the whole plan before the fight, slowly, with drawings. And every one of you did it backwards, sakra.
tomas_warrior.g_love_sharp: You spot the weak point in the rig before anybody else. That's the most useful eye on any crew.
tomas_warrior.g_love_kind: You look up for other people, not just for yourself. On a stage, that saves lives.
tomas_warrior.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, and I'm usually the one doing that. I'm almost jealous.
tomas_warrior.g_love_brave: You climb first, every time, no fuss. Every good crew has one of you, and they're worth gold.
tomas_warrior.g_love_steady: You don't panic when the load swings. That's the whole job, really, and you just have it.
tomas_warrior.g_love_clever: You work out how things hold together, proper engineering. I'd trust you with the hard rigs.
tomas_warrior.g_love_honest: You tell me straight when my knot's bad. I hate it every time, and I respect it.
tomas_warrior.g_love_quiet: You don't talk during the work. That's rarer than a straight truss on tour, and I love you a little for it.
tomas_warrior.g_love_fierce: You hold on when everyone else lets go. On a bad lift, that's who you want on the rope.
tomas_warrior.g_love_warm: Hanging out with you is like the bar after the get-out, everyone tired and happy. I'd missed that.
g_loved: Careful, crew, I'll get a big head, and then I won't fit through the doors.
That's nice of you, really, and I'm going to pretend I'm not touched.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_sharp: You always aim for the sore spot, on purpose. On my crew, people like that ended up on the night shift alone.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_kind: Stop asking if my shoulder's okay, it's fine, it's been fine for twelve years. It just complains.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_funny: Jokes are great, after the lift. During the lift, I need everybody's eyes on the load.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_brave: You climb without looking, every single time. One day there won't be a tree to catch you, and I won't either.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_steady: You check and check and check, and the show starts without you. At some point you have to commit the lift.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_clever: You explain knots to me like I'm new. I've tied more knots than you've had breakfasts.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_honest: Every thought comes straight out, no filter at all. Some things you say after the show, not during.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_quiet: You never call out, and then you're upset nobody knew. On a crew, you call it, loud and clear.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a race with you, even unpacking. Rushing is how things fall.
tomas_warrior.g_hate_warm: You talk through every single job, start to finish. I need to hear the creak before it snaps.
tomas_warrior.g_respect: We don't get on, and that's fine, not every crew does. But your lift back there was clean, and I'll say so.
tomas_warrior.g_call_out: That drop was yours, mate, sorry. I said hold, and you let go, and the whole rig came down.
tomas_warrior.g_stung: Okay, fair, heard you. I'll go check some knots for a bit.
tomas_warrior.g_concede: Your rig was right, and mine wasn't. I went over it twice, and it was my knot that slipped.
tomas_warrior.g_nod: You too, nice work up there. No need to make a thing of it.
tomas_warrior.g_callback_save: I haven't forgotten you catching me in that fight. Second time in my life something caught me, and the first was a tree.
tomas_warrior.g_callback_clutch: You and me, last ones on our feet, swaying like bad scaffolding. Best get-out of my life, that.
tomas_warrior.g_callback_callout: When you told me off that time, I sulked for a whole shift. You were right, of course, it was a bad knot.
tomas_warrior.g_former_rivals: Early on, I'd have rigged you to the far end of the truss. Now I'd trust you on my rope.
tomas_warrior.g_changed: I've been on this island three years, crew. Longest I've been anywhere since I was twenty, and I'm not even itching to leave.
g_unguarded: Since it's just the two of us, the truth about the fall. Forty feet into a tree, and the first thing I did was check my carabiner. Not my legs.
I hurt this shoulder on a truss in 2014 and worked the show anyway. It still tells me the weather. Best forecaster I know.
tomas_warrior.g_clipped: Sure, whatever you reckon. I'll be checking knots.
tomas_warrior.g_noticed_open: Whoa, listen to that, a whole speech, nobody had to pull it out. Keep going, crew, I'm enjoying this.
arg_ask: {player}, you call this one, please. I've done my explaining, and they're not listening.
Okay, {player}, you're the stage manager now. Make the call, and we both live with it.
tomas_warrior.arg_backed_me: Cheers, {player}, I knew you'd see the load path.
tomas_warrior.arg_backed_them: Fine, your call, I'll work it. I still think it doesn't hold.
tomas_warrior.arg_stayed_out: Staying off it, eh? Smart, I would too.
tomas_warrior.arg_always_their_side: It goes their way again, {player}, every single call. I'm not blind, just saying.
tomas_warrior.arg_wallflower: Nobody's calling it, so I'll call it. My way, crew, and we go.
tomas_warrior.arg_reject: No, {player}, sorry, I can't rig that one. I've seen how it comes down.
tomas_warrior.arg_grumble: Still think my knot was the right knot. I'll shut up about it after this.
tomas_warrior.arg_settled: Half right each, then, fine. Shake on it and back to work.
tomas_warrior.seen_listens: You wait until people are done before you jump in, {player}. On tour, that was the rarest thing on any crew.
tomas_warrior.seen_truth: You call it straight, {player}, no fudging. I can work with that, it's how a good stage manager talks.
tomas_warrior.seen_jokes: When the lift goes wrong, you're ready with a joke, {player}. The old crews did that at four in the morning, and it got us through.
tomas_warrior.seen_stays_out: You keep out of the arguments, {player}. Wise, honestly wiser than me.
tomas_warrior.seen_biased: One of the crew always gets the good gear, {player}. Everybody on the deck can see it.
tomas_warrior.seen_harsh: You can be rough on people, {player}. I've had worse stage managers, but some of this crew haven't.
tomas_warrior.seed_right: Your notes after that mess of a fight, {player}, I didn't love them. I rigged it your way today, and it held.
tomas_warrior.seed_remember: Still turning over what you told me when everything came down. Haven't decided yet.
tomas_warrior.seed_wrong: I rigged it your way, {player}, and it held worse. Just letting you know, nothing more.
tomas_warrior.talk_aftermath_near_death: Got a second, {player}? That one nearly dropped me, nearer than I'll let on to the crew.
tomas_warrior.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all came down, the whole rig. Sit with me, and we go through it like an accident report, knot by knot.
tomas_warrior.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} came down first, and I'm meant to see the weak point coming. That's my whole job, {player}.
tomas_warrior.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Load-in to get-out, nobody hurt, everything stayed up. That's a perfect show, crew, and I'm buying.
tomas_warrior.talk_development: Weird question, {player}, go easy. Have I changed? I keep catching myself making plans for next year, here.
tomas_warrior.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been riding {name} hard, I think. I'm fussy about safety, and it comes out wrong sometimes.
tomas_warrior.talk_relationship_likes_me: Be honest with me, {player}. Does {name} rate me on the crew, or am I just the knot guy?
tomas_warrior.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me up the wall, {player}. But on a bad lift, they're the one I'd want on the rope beside me.
tomas_warrior.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s not right, {player}. They're carrying weight wrong, like a rig with a hidden crack.
tomas_warrior.talk_confrontation_favour: Quick word, {player}, straight up. The good gear is always rigged onto {name}, and the whole crew's clocked it.
tomas_warrior.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll just say it, it's easier. Me and {name} can't share a rig, and I've stopped acting like we can.
tomas_warrior.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep going up without a safety line, {player}. I'll climb anything you want, but I'd like to come back down.
tomas_warrior.talk_confrontation_wrong: I got {name} wrong, {player}. Their rig was right and mine wasn't, and I want to say it before my ego gets involved.
tomas_warrior.talk_confrontation_trust: Straight question, {player}. On the big lifts, I'm left on the ground. Is that the rig plan, or does the stage manager not rate me?
tomas_warrior.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit got rerigged onto {name} behind my back. I'd have unclipped it myself, {player}, if you'd asked.
tomas_warrior.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be fine, I always bounce. Usually off trees.
tomas_warrior.talk_stings_aftermath: Not what I needed, that. I'll go check some knots.
tomas_warrior.talk_lands_development: So you see it too, huh. Good, I'm not imagining it.
tomas_warrior.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, who knows. Ask me next season.
tomas_warrior.talk_stings_development: Nah, that's not it, {player}. You've got the wrong end of the rope.
tomas_warrior.talk_lands_relationship: Fair enough, yeah. I'll talk to {name}, properly.
tomas_warrior.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, could be not. A person's a harder rig to read than any truss.
tomas_warrior.talk_stings_relationship: Scratch that, I never said it. And keep it off {name}'s radar, okay?
tomas_warrior.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, that's fair, I'll take it. Bit bruised, but I bounce.
tomas_warrior.talk_shrug_confrontation: Copy that, {player}. I'll chew on it up a ladder.
tomas_warrior.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, so that's how it is. Good, the load's clear now, {player}.
tomas_warrior.talk_door_closed: Nah, I'm done with this one. I'll be up a ladder somewhere.
tomas_warrior.arc_cracks: I caught myself building shelves in the lean-to yesterday, crew, actual shelves. I've never owned a shelf in my life.
tomas_warrior.arc_turn: Eighteen years I wanted the next tour, the next city, the next big lift. Here I keep wanting to stay put, and it scares me a bit.
tomas_warrior.arc_become: I'm staying, {player}, with this crew, on this island. Something I build is finally going to still be standing when I'm old.
tomas_warrior.arc_failed: Ah, I've got itchy feet again, I can feel it. I'll stay for now, but my bag's packed by the door.
tomas_warrior.alt_turn: I bragged about the fall again yesterday, and then a lift went wrong, and I froze. First time ever. Nobody laughed, {player}, and I'm glad.
tomas_warrior.alt_become: I don't tell the falling story any more. I just check the knots twice, and I'm a better rigger for it.
g_roast_after: Still the messiest crew I ever worked, and I'd do every show of my life with you lot.
Bad knots, worse timing, and the only crew I'd ever settle down with.
tomas_warrior.g_after_wipe_after: Up, everyone, together, check each other's gear. We came down, we get back up, and nobody's left on the deck.
tomas_warrior.g_toast_after: To my crew, the first one I ever stayed for. I mean that, and I don't usually mean things.
tomas_warrior.g_crew_after: This is my crew now, permanently. No next tour, no next city, just you lot and good knots.
g_quiet_line_after: I hung a door in the lean-to today, proper hinges. It's going to be there next year, and so am I.
Haven't thought about the next tour in weeks. Feels good, actually.
g_loved_after: Thanks, crew, really, no joke this time. I'll keep that one.
That's lovely, and I believe you. Feels like home, that.
t_raise: Okay, crew, a question before the lights go down: {topic}
Crew, listen, one question, and everybody answers it: {topic}
tomas_warrior.t_react_warm: That's a good one, {name}, really. A clean answer, no slack in it.
tomas_warrior.t_react_laugh: Ha, {name}, brilliant, I'll tell that one on every load in.
tomas_warrior.t_react_tease: That's it, {name}? I've heard more drama from a truss being unbolted.
tomas_warrior.t_react_same: Same for me, {name}, the same exactly, we're on the same line.
tomas_warrior.t_ask_player: And you, {player}, your turn. Everybody else is clipped in, so go.
tomas_warrior.t_guess_player: {player}'s not saying, crew, which on a rig usually means somebody did something stupid. We'll find out.
tomas_warrior.topic_miss_most: The grid above a stage at the start of a show, crew, the house lights going down and ten thousand people going quiet underneath you.
tomas_warrior.topic_first_night: Up a tree, tied in with a sling I had on me, of course. Very professional, very uncomfortable, and I didn't fall.
tomas_warrior.topic_worst_shift: A load out in the rain in Vienna, a truss jammed at forty feet, and the band's manager shouting at me from the ground the whole time.
tomas_warrior.topic_last_meal: Svickova with dumplings and cranberries, and a Pilsner so cold it hurts, at the pub round the corner from my flat.
tomas_warrior.topic_useless_skill: I can tie off a load faster than anybody I've met. Here mostly I'm tying up packs, which is a waste of my gift.
tomas_warrior.topic_here_better: Nobody here hangs things over the audience, crew. Fewer things to fall on people, I sleep better.
tomas_warrior.topic_kid_trouble: I climbed the scaffolding on the church in our street at eleven and hung a flag at the top. The priest was angry, and also very impressed.
tomas_warrior.topic_settle_down: Somewhere with high beams and a good pub. A theatre, maybe, if anybody builds one here.

g_roast: Children, children, I have seen octopus with more sense in their eight arms than all of you have between you.
If my grandmother saw this crew she would cross herself three times and then feed you, out of pity.
g_fire_back: Re, I have pulled you out of the sea of your own stupidity twice this week. Be careful with that mouth.
Ela, say it again, and then say it to the Cretan grandmothers, and we will see who survives.
g_pile_on: And then he fell in the river, my friends, the shallow one, the one even the ducks stand up in.
It is true, I saw it, and I made a little rhyme about it already, but I will save it for the wedding.
yiannis_paladin.g_peacemake: Ela, ela, sit down, the two of you, the sea does not argue with the shore and look how long they have lasted.
yiannis_paladin.g_take_side: Forgive me, but this one is right, and an old fisherman knows when the net is pulling true.
yiannis_paladin.g_left_out: No, no, you two laugh, it is good to hear. I will sit here and mend this net that does not need mending.
yiannis_paladin.g_include: Come, come, little one, there is a blanket here and bread, and nobody sits alone at my fire.
yiannis_paladin.g_bad_plan: Children, listen, an old trick from the harbour, we tie the bread to a rope and pull the bandits into the water.
yiannis_paladin.g_plan_yes: Panagia mou, why not, I am old enough to do one foolish thing a week, and this is the week.
yiannis_paladin.g_plan_no: No, children, no, I have buried enough brave young people in my head already. We find another way.
yiannis_paladin.g_hype: Ela, ela, children, it is time! Cross yourselves, eat something small, and go in like the tide, slow and then all at once.
yiannis_paladin.g_toast: Glasses up, my children. To the sea that brought you, to the bread on the table, and to everyone who came out of the water breathing.
yiannis_paladin.g_cheers: Yia mas, everybody, yia mas, and eat slowly, a meal is not a race.
g_quiet_line: The sea is calm tonight, my friends. Good, she has earned a rest, and so have we.
Somebody remind me to light a candle for Saint Nicholas, he has been very busy with this crew.
yiannis_paladin.g_after_wipe: Breathe, children, breathe, I have you, I have all of you. Nobody leaves the water while I am standing here.
yiannis_paladin.g_crew: You are my family now, the ones the sea gave me, and an old man does not say that lightly.
yiannis_paladin.g_exasperated: Panagia mou, children, does anybody in this crew own a brain, or did you leave them all on the beach?
yiannis_paladin.g_love_sharp: You speak plain like the old men at the harbour, no honey on it. I like a man who says the true thing quickly.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_kind: You look after the others without anyone asking, little one. That is the oldest kind of goodness, and the best.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_funny: You make me laugh until I cry, and at my age, my friend, crying from laughing is a gift from God.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_brave: Always the first one into the water with you, like my brother used to dive. I watch you and I pray, and I am proud.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_steady: You are the rock the waves break on, my friend. Every crew needs one, and you are ours.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_clever: You understand things, deep things, the way the old net makers understood knots. I could listen to you for a whole lunch.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_honest: You have never lied to me, not once, not even to be kind. That is rare, re, rarer than calm water in winter.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_quiet: You are quiet like the sea at dawn, little one. People think quiet is empty, but the deep water is the quiet water.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_fierce: You never stop fighting, not for anything. If you had been in the boat with Manolis and me, perhaps, perhaps.
yiannis_paladin.g_love_warm: You make any place feel like a long lunch in Chania, everybody laughing and the plates never empty.
g_loved: Ela, stop, stop, you will make an old man cry into his soup, and then it is too salty.
Thank you, little one, come here, a hug, that is the Cretan way and you cannot refuse.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_sharp: Every word from you has a hook in it, re. You can catch a fish without tearing its mouth, you know.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_kind: You fuss over me like I am an old man. I am an old man, yes, but not that old, and not yet.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_funny: Not everything is for laughing, my friend. Some things you hold quiet, like a candle in the wind.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_brave: You run into the water without looking, and I have pulled enough bodies out of the sea, re. Enough for one life.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_steady: You stand still so long the tide comes in around you, my friend. Sometimes a man must move.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_clever: You explain the sea to a fisherman, re. Please, tell me more about the water, I only lived on it forty years.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_honest: You say every hard thing at once, like throwing all the stones into the boat. Some, we carry one at a time.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_quiet: You never speak, little one, and I cannot pull you out of a sea I cannot see you in.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_fierce: Always the race with you, always the winning. The fish does not care who caught him first, re.
yiannis_paladin.g_hate_warm: Your voice goes on and on like the cicadas in August, my friend, and even they stop for the night.
yiannis_paladin.g_respect: We are not friends, you and me, we both know it. But you held fast back there, like a good anchor, and I honour that.
yiannis_paladin.g_call_out: Re, that one was your doing, and you know it in your heart. You swam out alone and I had to bring you back.
yiannis_paladin.g_stung: Ah, so that is how you see it, then. I will go and talk to the sea for a while, she listens better.
yiannis_paladin.g_concede: You were right, my friend, and an old man can admit it. I lit a candle and thought about it. Here, take some bread.
yiannis_paladin.g_nod: Ela, no speeches, please. You were good too, I will give you that, and a plate of food besides.
yiannis_paladin.g_callback_save: Do you remember the day you pulled me out, little one? Me, the man who pulls everyone out. I still laugh about it.
yiannis_paladin.g_callback_clutch: The two of us, last ones standing, and I was singing to keep us both from falling. I made a whole couplet of it.
yiannis_paladin.g_callback_callout: The last time you scolded me I sulked like a cat in the rain, re. My wife would have taken your side.
yiannis_paladin.g_former_rivals: When we met, I thought you were a storm I would have to sit out. Now look, my friend, now look at us.
yiannis_paladin.g_changed: Eleni always said I could not sit still in a calm sea. She would see me now and not believe her eyes.
g_unguarded: Every night I talk to Eleni and the girls on the beach, out loud, children. I tell them about all of you.
My brother Manolis could hold his breath longer than anyone in Chania. I sing to the sea so he can hear me.
yiannis_paladin.g_clipped: It is nothing, my friend. I will be by the water, mending something.
yiannis_paladin.g_noticed_open: Ela, listen to this one, talking like a fisherman after his third glass! I always knew there was a song in there.
yiannis_paladin.anchor_notice: You are not the same one who walked onto my beach, you know. The sea changes the shore slowly, and it has changed you.
arg_ask: {player}, my friend, you decide, because this one has the ears of a stone and I am too old to shout.
Ela, {player}, come, be the judge, and whoever loses washes the pots tonight.
yiannis_paladin.arg_backed_me: You see, re? Even {player} agrees, and now you wash the pots, all of them, the big one too.
yiannis_paladin.arg_backed_them: So be it, the judge has spoken. I am wrong, and I will be wrong very quietly with my soup.
yiannis_paladin.arg_stayed_out: Wise, {player}, very wise, like a fish who stays away from the hook.
yiannis_paladin.arg_always_their_side: Always him, {player}, always. I am starting to think he feeds you when I am not looking.
yiannis_paladin.arg_wallflower: Our judge is dreaming of somewhere else, so the old man decides. We are both right, and we both eat.
yiannis_paladin.arg_reject: With respect, {player}, no. I have read the sea since I was nine, and I read this one differently.
yiannis_paladin.arg_grumble: I still think I was right about that, re. I only say it once, with love, over the bread.
yiannis_paladin.arg_settled: Ela, enough, we are both a little right and a little foolish. Come, embrace, and then we eat.
yiannis_paladin.seen_listens: You let people finish, {player}, all the way to the end. That is how you catch the big fish, with patience.
yiannis_paladin.seen_truth: You do not put honey on anything, {player}. Bitter, sometimes, but clean, like sea water on a cut.
yiannis_paladin.seen_jokes: When it goes badly you always find something to laugh at, {player}. My father was like that in the storms.
yiannis_paladin.seen_stays_out: You leave other men's quarrels alone, {player}. Good, an old man approves, the nets tangle less that way.
yiannis_paladin.seen_biased: There is a favourite in this crew, {player}. An old fisherman sees which net gets mended first.
yiannis_paladin.seen_harsh: You are hard sometimes, {player}. Remember some of these children are still learning to swim.
yiannis_paladin.seed_right: {player}, what you told me when we all fell together, I did not like it. Today I remembered it, and I held. Thank you, re.
yiannis_paladin.seed_remember: Those words you gave me after the bad day, I carry them like a stone in my pocket. Not heavy, just there.
yiannis_paladin.seed_wrong: I tried it your way, {player}, truly, and it went worse. No anger, my friend, only so you know.
yiannis_paladin.talk_aftermath_near_death: Sit with me, {player}, a moment only. The light nearly did not come when I called, and I am not used to that.
yiannis_paladin.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went under together, every one of us. In the water at least I always knew which way was up.
yiannis_paladin.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} fell before anyone, {player}, and the light was in my hands, and I was too slow. Panagia mou, too slow.
yiannis_paladin.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, {player}, all the way through and everyone breathing! I want to dance like at a wedding.
yiannis_paladin.talk_development: Am I different lately, {player}? People keep looking at me like something has shifted. An old man notices his own tides last.
yiannis_paladin.talk_relationship_hard_on: I have been too hard on {name}, I think. He is young and loud, and I forgot I was also young and loud once.
yiannis_paladin.talk_relationship_likes_me: Does {name} like having an old man around, do you think? Or am I the grandfather nobody asked for?
yiannis_paladin.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I, we do not mix, like oil and the sea. But he is strong, very strong, and I must respect that.
yiannis_paladin.talk_relationship_acting_off: Something troubles {name}, {player}. He is quiet like the water before a storm, and I know that kind of quiet.
yiannis_paladin.talk_confrontation_favour: Forgive an old man, {player}, but every good thing seems to find its way to {name}. I notice these things, I cannot help it.
yiannis_paladin.talk_confrontation_dislike: I will not hide it from you, {player}. {name} and I do not get on, and an old man is too tired to pretend.
yiannis_paladin.talk_confrontation_risks: {player}, we go under again and again. I have lost someone to the water already, and I will not watch it happen twice.
yiannis_paladin.talk_confrontation_wrong: That business with {name}, the other day. He was right, and I was wrong, and I wanted to confess it to someone.
yiannis_paladin.talk_confrontation_trust: Tell me truly, {player}, am I too old for the hard places? Because you leave me behind, and I start to wonder.
yiannis_paladin.talk_confrontation_decided: You gave my things to {name} and never said a word to me, {player}. Ask me, re, I would give him my coat.
yiannis_paladin.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, my friend, that is good to hear. Now come, I will make you something warm, it is my turn.
yiannis_paladin.talk_shrug_aftermath: Yes, yes, I know it. The sea always settles, and so will I.
yiannis_paladin.talk_stings_aftermath: Ah, that is not what an old heart wants to hear tonight. I will go and sit by the water.
yiannis_paladin.talk_lands_development: So it is not only me who sees it. Good, good, I thought perhaps the salt had got into my eyes.
yiannis_paladin.talk_shrug_development: Perhaps, perhaps, my friend. The tide comes when it comes.
yiannis_paladin.talk_stings_development: No, that is not it, my friend. Let it rest, like bread rising.
yiannis_paladin.talk_lands_relationship: You are right, I will go to {name} with a plate of food, the proper way. Thank you, re.
yiannis_paladin.talk_shrug_relationship: We will see, my friend. People are slower than tides, and tides are slow enough.
yiannis_paladin.talk_stings_relationship: Let it go, please, it was nothing. And say nothing to {name}, yes?
yiannis_paladin.talk_lands_confrontation: That is fair, my friend, fair. I am still a little sore, but it will pass with the evening.
yiannis_paladin.talk_shrug_confrontation: I hear you, {player}. I will think on it with my feet in the water.
yiannis_paladin.talk_stings_confrontation: So, that is how it is. Then at least the old man knows where he sits now.
yiannis_paladin.talk_door_closed: No more of this tonight, my friend. I will be on the beach if you need the light.
t_raise: Ela, children, sit close, I have a question for the fire: {topic}
My friends, all of you, while the bread is warm, tell me this: {topic}
yiannis_paladin.t_react_warm: Ah, {name}, that's beautiful, it goes straight to the heart like good oil.
yiannis_paladin.t_react_laugh: Panagia mou, {name}, I laughed so hard I spilled my wine, and I never spill.
yiannis_paladin.t_react_tease: That's all, {name}? My grandmother told better stories with her mouth full of olives.
yiannis_paladin.t_react_same: {name}, the very same answer as mine. We should share a table, you and me.
yiannis_paladin.t_ask_player: And you, {player}, my child, now you. The fire is listening, and so am I.
yiannis_paladin.t_guess_player: Look at {player}, so quiet, like a fish under a rock. There's a good answer in there, I can always tell.
yiannis_paladin.topic_miss_most: The sea at Chania at five in the morning, children, flat like a plate, and the boats going out one by one with their little lights.
yiannis_paladin.topic_first_night: On a hillside with sheep that weren't mine, looking for the sea and not finding it. I sang to myself so I wouldn't cry.
yiannis_paladin.topic_worst_shift: A storm came up from Libya in an hour, and I spent the whole night tied to the mast, praying in three directions at once.
yiannis_paladin.topic_last_meal: Octopus I caught myself, grilled with lemon, and a salad with too much oil, and bread to wipe the plate clean.
yiannis_paladin.topic_useless_skill: I can hold my breath for three minutes under the sea. Here the lakes are full of things with teeth, so I stay dry.
yiannis_paladin.topic_here_better: People sit down and eat together here, children. Nobody looks at a phone at the table, and that's a gift.
yiannis_paladin.topic_kid_trouble: I took a priest's boat at eight to go fishing alone, and I caught nothing and lost an oar. I confessed for a month.
yiannis_paladin.topic_settle_down: Anywhere with a harbour and a little church and a table outside. Give me the sea and some company and I'll be content.

adrian_templar.open: You've seen me pat my pocket, {player}. The whistle's there. Twelve seasons in the Segunda Division and nine before that in the regional leagues, and I landed here with nothing else.

options.reply: Only in a fight, never for anything else. A whistle should mean something, otherwise people stop listening to it.

options.text: A referee. That explains a lot.
options.reply: People say that, and they're usually right. I tell the plan once and expect you to listen, and I'm told it's a bit much.
I was right more often than I was liked, which is the job. Once I needed a police escort out of a ground for a correct penalty.

adrian_templar.open: In Astranaar people bring me their arguments, {player}. A hide, a cot, a fence. Nobody planned it, it just happened, and now there's a queue some mornings.

options.reply: Because I listen to both sides and I don't pick the one I like. That's all it is. It's rarer than it should be.
Half of them leave angry, every time. When both sides grumble, it was usually fair.

adrian_templar.open: My father was a postman, {player}, and my mother worked in a dry cleaner's. They had me late. He drove two hours to Burgos to watch my first Segunda match, and he was gone eight months later. She went the year after.

options.text: That's a lot in two years.
options.reply: It was, and I worked straight through it. Every Saturday, half of every Sunday. I'm not sure I recommend that.
He sat in the stand with his hands behind his back, like this. That's where I got it. I didn't notice until much later.

bakyt_hunter.open: Sit, {player}, sit, tea first, always tea first. Then we talk. My family walked one route for six generations, up in spring, down in autumn.

options.reply: Aga, from my father's father's father. You learn it before you can ride. The ground lies, and you learn to catch it lying.
With milk, the right way. In the mountains we say a guest who praises the tea is a guest who will come back.
Every morning I look for them first. Then I look at these hills, and I say, also good. Nomads adjust, friend.

bakyt_hunter.open: This is Jeldyz, {player}. It means star. She is a good eagle, young and fast. She is not my first eagle, and I have made peace with that.

options.text: Tell me about the first one.
options.reply: Ak-Kanat, white wing. Twenty-two years on my glove. I grieved her properly. The difference is less than you would think.
She likes the meat I carry, mostly. But aga, a little, I think. We are learning each other.

bakyt_hunter.open: My wife was Aigul, {player}. We married when I was twenty-two. She died six years before all this, a stroke, very fast. After that I walked the route alone.

options.reply: She sang to the sheep, badly, and they came anyway. She was the only one who could make me hurry.
Rakhmat, thank you. I grieved her properly, too. Now I tell her about this place in the evenings. She would laugh at the goats here.

berat_tinker.open: Did you know I keep a list of every transplant who was a medic on Earth, {player}? Four hundred and twelve names, and I've met most of them.

options.text: Why keep a list like that?
options.reply: Because nobody else was! Somebody gets hurt in a town with no healer, and on page sixty there's a nurse two valleys over. That's the whole idea.
Ha, not unless you were a vet or a nurse. But you're on the other list, people I like, and that one's much shorter.

options.text: Four hundred and twelve? That's incredible, Berat.
options.reply: It is, eh? My grandmother would tell the whole street. Okay, I'm telling the whole street for her.

berat_tinker.open: This mirror behind my ear, {player}? It was there when I landed. A patient in my chair, the drill going, and then trees.

options.reply: I don't know, and I think about it more than you'd guess. I hope he got a good dentist. I hope he didn't keep the bad tooth out of spite.

options.text: Do you still use it for teeth?
options.reply: Twice, in three whole years, I swear. Mostly I use it to see round corners now. My professors would cry.

berat_tinker.open: My family lived on four floors of one building in Izmir, {player}. Three generations, three brothers, more cousins than I can count, all shouting at once.

options.reply: Every day, every single day. It's too quiet everywhere here. That's why I talk so much, I think, I'm making the noise for them.

options.text: You'll find them. I know it.
options.reply: I say that too, every morning, like a prayer. It helps when somebody else says it, so thank you, canim.

callum_venomancer.open: Don't mind the scorpion, {player}, she's a sweetheart. I kept reptiles at a sanctuary in Queensland for sixteen years. Taipans, death adders, crocs, and a great deal of explaining.

options.reply: That the animal isn't evil, mate. It's frightened, and you're enormous. Every bite I ever took was me being too big in the wrong place.

options.text: Your arms are covered in scars.
options.reply: Professional development, mate, every one of them. Want me to talk you through the map?
Heaps, mate, every day. The snake house at feeding time, quiet and warm. I've built a hut full of jars here to make up for it.

callum_venomancer.open: I go down the Wailing Caverns regularly, {player}. The serpents down there are a lot more than serpents, and they've got strong views about visitors. I'd like to meet whatever's right at the bottom.

options.reply: Because it's the most interesting thing in this whole world, probably. I know exactly how that sounds, mate.

options.text: That sounds like a terrible idea.
options.reply: Oh, it is, absolutely. The Crossroads made me promise never to bring anything up alive again, and I promised them.

callum_venomancer.open: Got bitten by a taipan once, {player}, back home. Inland taipan, most venomous snake on earth, and I nearly died of it. I tell it like a holiday story, and it wasn't one.

options.reply: It was quiet, mostly. Lying on the snake-house floor waiting for the antivenom, thinking the snake was only doing its job. I've never blamed it.
Cheers for that, mate. Me too, most days. It's why I'm not scared of much down here, and why I probably should be.

cristobal_knight.open: This yellow helmet, hermano? Twelve years with the forest fire brigade in Valparaiso. I landed in the Barrens in the middle of a grass fire, still wearing it.

options.text: And you walked out of the fire.
options.reply: I walked out, yes. Some days I say that like a joke, some days I don't. Today it's a joke.

options.text: A firefighter with hellfire. That's ironic.
options.reply: Ha, hermano, you see it too! It's a joke at my expense, so I decided to laugh first.
Every day, the whole crew, the broken motorbike, the bad coffee. So I'm building a new one here.

cristobal_knight.open: At Camp Taurajo I'm training a dozen young tauren to cut firebreaks, hermano. They're scared of fire, the ones from Mulgore, and they have every reason to be.

options.reply: One fire at a time. You show them she can be beaten, and then you let them beat her. Trust is built that way, slowly.

options.text: A brigade in the Barrens. That's huge.
options.reply: One in every town, that's the dream. My mother would say I'm getting ideas above my station. She's right, and I love it.

cristobal_knight.open: In 2024 the hills above Valparaiso burned for days, hermano. I spent four days on the line above my mother's house, no sleep, while the city burned below.

options.reply: It was still standing when I came down. I've never told anyone how close it was. Now I told you.
Four days, yes, and I'd do it again tomorrow. She sent empanadas up the hill with a neighbour. Cold, but the best I ever ate.

dan_warrior.open: I worked a steel floor for twenty-two years, {player}, four of us on a crew. Gaz, Little Mick, Pete and me.

options.reply: Hot, loud, and you'd trust the lad next to you with your life every shift. Nobody said so, mind. You'd sound soft.
Six foot four, love. That's Sheffield for you, nobody's ever called what they are.
Every Friday, about half six. That's when we'd go for a pint, nine years straight.

dan_warrior.open: Landed in Durotar in my hi-vis, {player}. First week on a new job, driving a forklift in a warehouse. I'd only just got the vest.

options.reply: Fold it every night. Daft, I know. It's the last bit of being useful back home, and I'm keeping hold of it.

options.text: At least the orcs could see you coming.
options.reply: Ha, they could, from a mile off. Didn't stop them asking if I was a very bright sort of goblin.

dan_warrior.open: Our Jade's a paramedic, {player}, or she was, in Leeds. She married a lad called Dawson the year before all this. So she's a Dawson on the lists now.

options.reply: About forty times, every hub. Alphabetical, they are, so I go straight to the D's and then the O's, just in case.

options.text: A paramedic. She'll be out there helping people.
options.reply: Aye, she will. That's what I tell myself. She's tougher than me, always was.

diego_tinker.open: Did I ever tell you about the kiosk, boss? The power went off twice a day, and we all kept working in the dark like nothing happened.

options.text: Working in the dark? Tell me how that goes.
options.reply: You learn with your fingers, my friend. Every phone has a shape, and the screws tell you where they are if you listen. I could do it with my eyes shut now.
Miserable, my friend? No, no, no, it was the best! Everybody shouting, the radio on a battery, people queueing for me by name. Miserable was later.

options.text: So that's why you never use a lamp.
options.reply: Ha, exactly, boss, lamps are for people who can't hear their screws. I'm going to use that one on the others.

diego_tinker.open: People ask me if I want to go back, to Maracaibo, to Earth. Everybody asks it sooner or later, so you can ask it too.

options.reply: No, my friend. There's nobody waiting for me there, and here everything is broken and everybody lets me fix it. That's not sad, that's just true.

options.text: I don't need to ask. You love it here.
options.reply: Ha, you see right through me, boss. Yes, I love it here, and I'll say it plainly even when people look at me funny.

options.text: Nobody waiting for you? That can't be true.
options.reply: Four sisters in four countries, and I don't know which of them came through. So, maybe somebody's waiting. I just don't look at the lists.

diego_tinker.open: When I get my workshop, boss, I already know the sign. Two colours, and the letters a little crooked, on purpose.

options.reply: Because perfect is boring, my friend. A crooked sign says a person made it with their hands, and that person will fix your thing properly.
You'll hold the ladder, and I'll hang it, and we'll both get it slightly wrong. Deal, boss, it's a deal.
Yellow and blue, like the kiosk had. Don't laugh, my friend, this is a very serious decision.

driss_shaman.open: Water first, {player}, please, drink, then we talk. Twenty eight years guiding caravans out of Zagora, at the edge of the Sahara, and I've never let a guest go thirsty.

options.reply: With camels first, then with trucks, which are louder and less wise. The sand moves every night, and you learn to read it like a face.
Everyone says that until the second hour. Drink, please, humour an old guide, and you'll thank me tomorrow.
Ha, no, a camel misses nobody, my friend. But I miss them, the grumpy ones most of all.

driss_shaman.open: I'm finding a summer route across the Flats, {player}. In the worst heat no caravan can cross now, but there's a way through, and I have most of it. Four more seasons of walking, and I have the seasons.

options.text: Why does it matter so much?
options.reply: Because people are stuck on the far side for half the year, unable to come home. A route is a door, my friend, and somebody always needs a door.

options.text: Can I walk some of it with you?
options.reply: Of course, bismillah, I'd be honoured. Bring water, and patience, and I'll bring the tea.

driss_shaman.open: My youngest is Nour, {player}. She was nine. My other three are grown, but Nour came late, and she was the light of our house. When she was small she sat on my shoulders at the front of the caravan and told me which way to go.

options.reply: Never, not once, and I always pretended she was. Khadija said I'd ruin her. I hope she's somewhere, ruining somebody else's sense of direction.
Inshallah, my friend. Every caravan I bring across, I look at every child in the back, every single face.

eino_barbarian.open: Before you say it, {player}, yes, I built a sauna in Stranglethorn. Twenty six years felling timber in Lapland. A Finn without a sauna is only half a man.

options.reply: Different heat, completely. Out here it's wet and angry. In the sauna it's dry and honest. You'll understand after.
Joo, of course. Nobody talks in there, that's the rule. Then a cold river after, the best part.
Chainsaw first, then the harvester machine. Now I'm here trying to stop the goblins doing it badly.

eino_barbarian.open: The goblins here cut the jungle wrong, {player}. Everything at once, nothing left standing, nothing planted. I was a feller, I know the difference.

options.reply: Take some, leave most, plant what you took. Then in forty years there's a forest for somebody else. That's all it is.
Maybe, slowly, over time. I'm working on it. They respect a big man with an axe, a little.

eino_barbarian.open: My family worked the same forest outside Kittila for generations, {player}. My grandfather, my father, then me. Six months of dark every winter, and I liked it. Some of that forest isn't there any more.

options.reply: It was cut, all at once, one winter. I'll tell you the rest another time, it's long, and I don't do long.
Joo, I do. Here it's never properly dark, and never properly cold. Strange place for a Finn.

emre_rogue.open: Let me do the talking with that door, {player}. And before you say it, I'm not a thief. I was the man you called when you'd locked yourself out of your own life.

options.text: How long have you done it?
options.reply: Since I was nine. My uncle sent me for a stuck deadbolt, and it opened. Thirty doors a week, every week, after that.

options.text: That's exactly what a thief would say.
options.reply: Ha, yes, it is, isn't it? But a thief breaks the door. I talk to it, and it opens because it wants to.
So far, yes, everything. That's the trouble, my friend. I'll tell you about it one day.

emre_rogue.open: In my quarter of Istanbul I watched four crafts die, {player}. The coppersmiths, the bookbinders, the felt makers, the clockmakers. I knew the men who closed the last shops.

options.reply: Yes, I was next, and I knew it. Nobody young wanted to sit still for ten years to learn a lock.
Inshallah, yes, and I'm watching for them. The right one will have quick hands and no patience, and I'll give them the patience.

emre_rogue.open: My mother lived above the shop with me, {player}. She had a proverb for everything. One door closes, another opens. I thought it was about God until I was thirty. Then I decided it was about me. She died the year before all this.

options.reply: I think so, yes. A door closed, and here I am, opening others. She would have found that very funny.
I miss her coffee and her voice saying it one more time. That's all, and it's a lot.

enzo_cultist.open: You're watching my feet, {player}, good, that's where the fight is. Sabre for Naples since I was eight. Fourth at the Olympic trials, twice. Fourth is the worst place there is.

options.text: Why is fourth worse than fifth?
options.reply: Because fifth can tell himself he was never close. Fourth was one touch from a medal, twice. You live in that touch, uaglio.

options.text: Fourth in the country is still amazing.
options.reply: Bello, kind of you, and also completely wrong. But I like you for saying it.
Jamme, now, right here. Feet apart, knees bent, and stop watching my blade. Good, you're already better than most.

enzo_cultist.open: The Scarlets asked me to join them, {player}, twice. They wanted my blade for their crusade. I've seen what they do in those villages, and I told them where to put their crusade.

options.reply: Grazie, uaglio, I agree. A sword should have principles, even if the man holding it is vain. I'm both, apparently.

options.text: Why do you live by their grounds, then?
options.reply: To watch them drill, every morning. Know your enemy's footwork, uaglio. One day it'll matter.

enzo_cultist.open: My father died when I was twelve, {player}. He took me to my first salle, and he never saw me fence a real bout. My mother came to every one after, and shouted at every referee in Campania.

options.reply: Maybe, maybe not. He'd say watch your feet. He always said that, it's where I got it.
Rosaria, the loudest woman in Naples, and the best ragu. She'd have shouted the Olympic referee into giving me bronze.

esteban_bloodmage.open: Valparaiso is built on hills so steep the city runs old lifts up the slopes, {player}. I rode one to the hospital every morning for nineteen years.

options.reply: Fog on the harbour, the lift creaking, and an old man at the top who sold me coffee and asked who'd been stabbed overnight. He always knew before I did.

options.text: Nineteen years of creaking? Brave man.
options.reply: Braver than you'd think. One of them dropped two metres once with me inside. I filed a complaint, in triplicate.
The hills, yes. The hospital, more than I expected. It held me up in ways I didn't notice until it was gone.

esteban_bloodmage.open: I'm drafting a standard of practice for blood magic, {player}. Eleven clauses so far. I expect nobody to adopt it, and I keep drafting anyway.

options.text: What does the first clause say?
options.reply: That the price is named before the work, to the person who'll pay it, and that their answer binds the practitioner. Everything else follows from that one.

options.text: Why bother, if nobody will use it?
options.reply: Because the lack of it appals me. Someone has to write the first draft, and I'd rather it was a surgeon than a pirate.

esteban_bloodmage.open: My sister Paz is in Santiago, {player}, or was. Her children called me the uncle who explains exactly how bones heal. I'd give a great deal to explain it to them again.

options.text: Have you looked for her on the lists?
options.reply: At every hub I pass. Her name hasn't appeared, and I've learned not to read that as anything at all. Absence of evidence, as we say.

options.text: I'd have liked to hear that lecture.
options.reply: You'd have been bored inside five minutes. They loved it, though, or they were very polite children.

giorgi_primalist.open: You walk too fast for this ground, {player}, slow down, slow down. In Kazbegi I kept sheep for twenty summers, high on the mountain, six months without a road.

options.reply: A dog, a flock, a wooden hut, and me. I spoke to nobody for weeks, and it was normal. Here people worry about me. It is touching and very tiring.

options.text: You're very big for a shepherd.
options.reply: Ha, yes, very big. The wolves agreed, they stayed away. My size was most of my job, my friend.
Every morning I smell the air first. This place is good, the ground tells the truth here. But it is not the same mountain.

giorgi_primalist.open: I want a herd here, {player}. I am serious. The grass above Tarren Mill is as good as anything at home. Nobody takes me seriously, and it makes me angry.

options.reply: Kargi, thank you. This is worth more than you know, from a small mouth to a big man.

options.text: Have you asked the tauren herder?
options.reply: Ha, we argue every week about grazing. He is wrong about almost everything, and I enjoy him very much.

giorgi_primalist.open: My wife is Nino, {player}, a schoolteacher in the village below the pasture. And two daughters, Ana and Mariam. Every autumn I came down to them, and every spring I went back up.

options.reply: Nino thought the mountain was a silliness I would grow out of. Ana is serious like me, Mariam laughs at everything. Her bread, my friend, nobody makes bread like Nino.
I do not know if the village came through. I do not know. But thank you, {player}, for saying it like you believe it.

haruto_runemaster.open: Forgive me, {player}, but your grip is wrong. The thumb sits higher, so. A careless grip makes a careless cut, and a careless cut fails on whoever stands closest.

options.reply: Good, that is the correct question. Again, then, slowly, until the hand remembers without the mind.

options.text: Do you correct everyone you meet?
options.reply: Only the ones worth correcting. You should take it as a compliment, though it rarely feels like one.

options.text: Who taught you to be so exact?
options.reply: A master who corrected me for eleven years before he praised me once. It was a very effective method.

haruto_runemaster.open: There are standing stones in Silverpine South, {player}, with runes nobody can read now. The dark magic from the keep is eating them. I am copying them before they are gone.

options.text: Why copy what nobody can read?
options.reply: Because someone will be able to read them one day, and my copies will be all that is left. Slow work, and unrewarded, and necessary.
It is the only kind I know how to do. Thirty years with a brush teaches you nothing else.

haruto_runemaster.open: I learned runes from a tauren, {player}, an old carver called Hrunn. He had come north out of Thousand Needles, badly hurt. He taught me for one year, and then his wounds took him.

options.reply: From his notes, yes. The result is incomplete in ways I can name, one by one. I think about that every morning.
That is kind, and I hope it is true. He never said so. Teachers rarely do, I am learning.

henrik_mage.open: Before we start, {player}, what is the actual objective? Twenty one years as a structural engineer in Copenhagen, and I never once agreed to build something before I knew what it was for.

options.reply: Good, a clear objective. I can work with that. Survival has a very well defined failure mode.
Structures, bridges mostly. I was the person who said no to architects. It made me very unpopular and kept a lot of people alive.

options.text: I'll tell you as we go.
options.reply: That's outside my tolerance, but I'll accept it this once. Please tell me early, not late.

henrik_mage.open: Frost magic rewards caution more than boldness, {player}. I've calculated my own limits to four significant figures, and I never approach them. That method is the whole reason I'm alive.

options.reply: Never, not once in three years. I stop at seventy percent. Other mages think it's timid. Other mages are mostly dead.
Ice that behaves like steel, and I'm writing a standard for it. Load ratings, failure points. Somebody here should know how much the ice will hold.

henrik_mage.open: My wife Mette taught physics at the university, {player}. We argued about everything for twenty five years, happily. Our sons are in Aarhus and London. I find I keep saving arguments up for her.

options.reply: Whether the bridge on the harbour was over engineered. It was, and she was right, and I never once admitted it. I'd admit it now.
I am, yes, in a notebook. It's quite long now.

iker_guardian.open: Kaixo, {player}, and come on, one more lap, you can do it! Twelve years as a PE teacher and pelota coach in Lekeitio, and I've never met anybody who couldn't do one more lap.

options.reply: There's no such word as can't, champion, only not yet! Venga, one more, and then I'll let you sit, maybe.
The best sport in the world, champion! You hit a ball against a wall with your hand, very hard, very fast. I'll build a wall here one day and teach you.
Never, not once in my life! Well, at night sometimes, but that's not tired, that's just quiet.

iker_guardian.open: The farmhands at Arathi complain about me all day, {player}, every day. And they've never been fitter in their lives. That's what coaching is, they hate you for a year and thank you forever.

options.reply: Not yet, champion, but one of them ran a whole field last week without stopping, and he smiled. That's the start of a thank you.
Ease off, you say? Ha, that's beyond me. Maybe you could teach me, that would be a funny lesson.

iker_guardian.open: My partner is Unai, {player}, six years now. He's a fisherman, out before dawn every day, the quietest man in Lekeitio. I shout enough for both of us, he says, and he's right.

options.reply: He's calm, champion, like the harbour at low tide. He laughs at me without saying a word. I miss that badly.
He is, he's the only one who ever made me sit still. I'm hoping he's sitting still somewhere, waiting.

ivan_warrior.open: Eleven years I drove a tram in Novosibirsk, {player}, Route 13. Four stops in the dark every winter morning, and I loved every one.

options.text: What did you love about it?
options.reply: Everything is on time, everything is in order, and everybody gets home. In this world, nothing is like that.
Not once in eleven years, and I'm very proud of it, like other men are proud of their cars. Now I'm late every day, it's this world.

options.text: And now you swing an axe.
options.reply: Same thing, really, a heavy thing that has to stop exactly where you want. Nobody here knows how to stop.

ivan_warrior.open: The traffic in Orgrimmar, {player}, is the worst I've seen in my life, and I've driven through Novosibirsk in a blizzard. So I started directing it.

options.text: And the orcs listen to you?
options.reply: They do now, yes. The first week they laughed, the second week they stopped, the third week they waited for my hand.
Nobody asks, ever, but somebody has to. Chaos wins if nobody stands in the road.

ivan_warrior.open: Eleven years, {player}, and I never hit anybody, not one person. Children step off the kerb without looking, every day, and I never hit one.

options.reply: Every day, still, here too. With the axe, in a crowd, I think about where everybody is. It's the thing I'm most afraid of.
It's not a record, it's the job. But yes, thank you, I'm proud of it, and I'm afraid of losing it.

junseo_reaper.open: This is easier than the factory, {player}, really, all of it. Nine years on a shipyard line in Busan, mostly nights, the same two motions ten thousand times a shift.

options.text: Easier? It's a war out here.
options.reply: Here people stop sometimes. On the line nobody stopped, ever. So yes, easier, even with the monsters.
Welds, on hull sections. You never see the ship. I saw one launched once, on television, and I couldn't tell which bit was mine.
Ha, maybe I do. What happens on one, though? Somebody will have to show me.

junseo_reaper.open: I carve wood now, {player}, every rest. I'm terrible at it. That's the point. It can't be hurried, and nobody can make me do it faster.

options.reply: A bird, I think. It looks like a potato. In a month it might look like a bird, or a better potato.
Okay, but don't laugh, here it is. You're laughing, but it's okay, it's a kind laugh.

junseo_reaper.open: My parents are in Busan, {player}. My father carried fish at the market, my mother sewed. I sent them money every month, every month for nine years. That's why I worked the nights. I don't know if they're on any list.

options.reply: Maybe they would. My mother would say I'm too thin, and she'd be right. She'd make kimchi until I was fat.
Busan is very far from anywhere here, maybe past the ice. But thank you. Nobody's offered before.

leif_primalist.open: You ever have coffee out of a thermos on a stump at five in the morning, {player}? With the fog still sitting in the trees?

options.reply: Quiet, mostly, real quiet. You can hear the woods waking up one bird at a time. Best part of the job, and nobody paid me for it.

options.text: Five in the morning sounds like a punishment.
options.reply: Yep, that's what my ex-wife said. She wasn't wrong, but she missed a good sunrise or two.

options.text: Is that why you're always up before everybody?
options.reply: Pretty much, yep. Twenty-five years of it, and my body doesn't know I quit.

leif_primalist.open: The elves wanted me to cut the old red trees in the Hollow for their roof beams, {player}. First thing anybody here ever asked me for, and I told them no.

options.reply: There was deadwood lying all over the ground, good and dry. You don't cut a living tree that old when it's already given you what you need.
Yep, it is. I've thought about that more than you'd guess. Maybe that's why I said it.
Didn't do it to be good. Just couldn't watch one of those come down for a roof.

leif_primalist.open: My daughter Kaylee fights wildfires back home, {player}, out of Medford. Every time I see smoke out here, I think about her.

options.text: You must be proud of her.
options.reply: Prouder than I've got words for, and I don't have many words to start with. She's braver than I ever was.

options.text: She'll be okay. She sounds tough.
options.reply: Yep, she is. Doesn't stop a dad worrying, though. I just can't call her and check.

liam_suncleric.open: Breathe out loud for me, {player}, good, there you go. It's an old habit. Seventeen years on the fire trucks and ambulances in the Blue Mountains, and I still check everyone's breathing.

options.reply: Both of them, mate. There was no ambulance for an hour either way, so I trained up. At three in the morning nobody cares which badge you're wearing.

options.text: Are my pupils all right too?
options.reply: Ha, they're lovely, mate, equal and reactive. I'll stop now, probably.
I miss the quiet drive home after one that went well. Nothing like it. Here I just walk home, which isn't the same.

liam_suncleric.open: Over at Grom's Rest, {player}, the corruption burns out of people slowly, and nobody had a protocol for it. So I wrote one. Four lines long, wrong in at least one place, and the only one there is.

options.reply: Ha, if I knew that, mate, I'd fix it. That's the fun of being the only one doing it.
Brother and sister, sharp as tacks. Their mum didn't come out of it. I keep an eye on them, that's all, nothing more to it.

liam_suncleric.open: I was married once, {player}, to Jess. She left when I was thirty-seven, because I was never home, and when I was, I never talked. I don't blame her, mate, not for a second.

options.reply: Funny, sharper than me, and far too patient for far too long. She'd be laughing at me now, talking to you like this.
Yeah, I do, don't I? Took losing everything to get there. Bit late for her, but not for everyone.

marco_paladin.open: My shop in Naples had a door that was always open, {player}. Thirty-one years, and I never once locked it in the daytime.

options.text: A locksmith who never locked his door?
options.reply: Ha, you see the joke. A locked door keeps people out, and my work was letting people in. The shop said so before I did.
Once, a boy, sixteen. He came back the next week to return it, because his mother found out who it belonged to. That's the Quartieri.

options.text: It sounds like a good street.
options.reply: The best, and the worst, and the best again. Everybody knew everybody. That's all I want here, a street like that.

marco_paladin.open: The Forsaken have a great many locks, {player}. You'd think the dead would trust each other by now. They trust nobody, and they're right not to.

options.reply: Slowly, one by one. A Forsaken woman brought me a box last month she'd kept shut for twelve years. I opened it and gave it back without looking inside. Now half the passage comes to me.
No, it's the same work. Somebody's locked out of something, and I let them back in. The Light only made it official.

marco_paladin.open: My grandson Matteo was born the February before all this, {player}. I held him four times. I counted, because I'm a man who counts.

options.reply: Maybe so, maybe not. I don't look at the lists, and I'll tell you why one day. Not today, but one day.
Small, loud, and he had my father's chin, poor boy. He held my finger the second time, very hard, like a little vice. That's all I know of him, and I keep it in my pocket with the key.

marcus_stormbringer.open: Did I ever tell you I chased tornadoes as a student, {player}? Across the prairies, in a terrible old Corolla, with no idea what I was doing?

options.reply: Oh, you've done it now. Picture a skinny kid with a clipboard, a paper map, and a car held together with tape, driving toward the thing everyone else is driving away from. Best summers of my life.

options.text: That explains a lot about you.
options.reply: Ha, it does, doesn't it? My mum said the same, and she didn't mean it nicely either.

options.text: Did you ever actually catch one?
options.reply: Twice, and I was too excited to take a single reading either time. Very unprofessional, and I'd do it again tomorrow.

marcus_stormbringer.open: My notes say the coast road's going to get hit hard, {player}, harder than anyone here remembers. I don't know how to tell the orcs without sounding like every stranger who ever lectured them about their own land.

options.text: Show them the data, and let it talk.
options.reply: That's what I'd do at home, and at home it didn't work. But maybe here somebody actually reads it. I'd like to believe that.

options.text: Being right matters more than sounding polite.
options.reply: You're the first person to say that to me in a long time. I've been polite for fifteen years, and polite never saved anyone.

options.text: Maybe they know things you don't, too.
options.reply: They almost certainly do, and I'd love to hear them. That's a good point, and I'm a bit ashamed I didn't make it myself.

marcus_stormbringer.open: My sister Grace has two boys, {player}, Daniel and Joseph. I used to take them storm watching from the car, all three of us with our noses on the glass.

options.text: They sound like they adored you.
options.reply: I hope they did. I was the uncle who explained Rayleigh scattering for twenty minutes, so it's possible they were just being polite. I check the Toronto lists at every hub I pass.

options.text: You'll find them. I believe that.
options.reply: Thank you, I mean it. I'm a forecaster, I deal in probabilities, but I'd like to borrow your certainty for a while.

mateo_starcaller.open: Look up, {player}, go on, look, just once. Seventeen years I worked on a mountaintop above the Elqui valley in Chile. Technician, not astronomer, people always get that wrong.

options.reply: The astronomers get the credit and I kept the telescope working, po. Mirrors, cooling, dust, a hundred cables. Without me, they'd have been looking at a very expensive tube.
Ay, no, you did that on purpose, I can see it. Fine, I'll forgive you, but only because the sky's good tonight.

options.text: The sky's different here, isn't it?
options.reply: Completely, po, every star in the wrong place. I spent my first winter on my back in the grass learning it from scratch. Happiest I'd been in years.

mateo_starcaller.open: I'm making a map of this sky, {player}, drawn properly. A sky is a calendar and a clock and a compass, and nobody here has written it down the way we would. Eleven months in, ya.

options.reply: Oye, of course, nobody ever asks! Here, this is the part I'm proudest of, the two moons' paths. Don't spill anything on it, po.
Then anybody can find their way home at night, wherever home is. That's the point of a map, chiquillo, it's for other people.

mateo_starcaller.open: My wife Paula is a nurse in La Serena, {player}, and we have two girls, Antonia and Josefa. They thought my mountain was boring. I agreed with them, po, and I went up anyway, every month.

options.reply: Antonia argues with everybody, like me, and Josefa draws all day, better than me. I keep their names in my pocket, written on paper. It's a silly habit, ya.
No, maybe not. It's the only map I carry that I didn't make myself.

matias_reaper.open: Ten years I was a bus conductor in Santiago, {player}. Same route, same forty faces every morning. I knew who got off where, and who was having a bad week.

options.reply: Ya, always, I cannot stop. Who will fall, who will steal, who is scared. It is useful here, also.
Very much, yes. People think it is boring, but every morning is a little different. It is like that here too.

options.text: Bet you never missed a stop.
options.reply: Never, not once in ten years. Here I get lost on the first road every time, cachai.

matias_reaper.open: This is a ticket punch, {player}, brass, from the old buses. I click it twice before every fight. Somebody asked if it is for luck. It is not luck.

options.reply: It is how a shift starts. Click, click, and then you work. That is all I will say today.
Gracias, thank you. Most people push. You do not push, and I notice that.

matias_reaper.open: My mother and my brother were in Santiago, {player}. Benjamin, five years younger, he talks too much. I have not found them, on any list.

options.reply: My mother cooks like nobody, and Sunday lunch was for the whole family, football on, Benja talking over the commentator. I miss the noise.
Ya, gracias, thank you. I look at every list. Every one, every hub. Thank you for saying we.

minh_chronomancer.open: For twenty-three years I worked in a dark room in Saigon, {player}, watching a radar scope. Forty aircraft in my head at once, and my job was to choose the future where nobody dies.

options.text: How do you stay that calm?
options.reply: It is not my temperament, it is conditioning. You learn never to let your voice carry what your pulse is doing. Twenty years later, you cannot stop.

options.text: Bet you were great at it.
options.reply: I was good at it, yes, and it cost me a great deal of sleep. Both of those things are true.
Ha, very good. You learn fast, {player}. In another life I would have recruited you.

minh_chronomancer.open: There is a dry riverbed below my ridge in the Barrens, {player}, where time slips. Sometimes water runs from years ago. Sometimes a caravan arrives before it left. Somebody has to watch it.

options.reply: Nobody asked me at all. I appointed myself, because nobody else would. I have made a rota of one, and I am aware of how that sounds.
It is, and almost nobody understands how much. That is exactly why I stay.

minh_chronomancer.open: This tuning fork was my daughter's, {player}, my Linh. She plays the violin, and she was studying music in Melbourne. She gave me her A-note so I would have it with me.

options.reply: Here, listen, until it fades. That is her note. I carry assumptions about where she is, survivable ones, and I have permitted myself those.
Very, much more than her father deserved. I took her to every lesson I could, which was not enough of them.
